Yasuo

the Unforgiven
Mid laneTop laneBot lane

Top Yasuo is a lonely duelist: no support to cover you, a long lane, and a lot of melee bruisers who want to stand on you. You win by farming safely, using Wind Wall and your passive shield to dodge the worst trades, and turning a lead into a split-push that the enemy can't stop alone.

Nerfed in patch 26.22: His Q scales a little less with attack damage, so crit builds hit slightly softer.
  • Q AD ratio: 105% total AD → 100% total AD
All patch changes →

When to pick Yasuo

✗ Better as a counter-pick

Many popular bruisers beat him in a long lane, so pick him top only after you've seen the enemy top laner.

Pick into

  • Ranged top laners whose damage comes from projectiles, like Heimerdinger or Quinn
  • Slow tanks who can't punish short trades, like K'Sante
  • Teams with knock-ups you can follow up on, like Malphite or Gragas on your side
  • Enemy teams with lots of projectile ultimates Wind Wall can block

Avoid into

  • Bruisers with healing and long fights, like Darius or Aatrox
  • Champions with unblockable gap-closers and burst, like Camille
  • Hard point-and-click crowd control that locks you down
  • Teams that already have a lot of fragile, scaling picks with no frontline

Great teammates

MalphiteHis ultimate knocks up several enemies, giving you a huge Last Breath.
GragasHis body slam and ultimate both knock enemies into the air.
DianaHer ultimate pulls enemies together, perfect for a follow-up Steel Tempest tornado.

Your team needs: A frontline and at least one ally knock-up, so you aren't the only one starting fights.

How to read the enemy team → · Practice drafting →

Strengths

  • Your passive shield and Wind Wall let you take short trades that ranged top laners can't punish
  • Sweeping Blade through minions gives you more mobility than most top laners
  • Strong split-pusher once you have Blade of The Ruined King and Immortal Shieldbow
  • The top quest gives you a free Unleashed Teleport to join fights even without taking Teleport

Weaknesses

  • Melee bruisers with sustain and crowd control (like Darius) beat you in long fights
  • No partner to help when the enemy jungler ganks
  • Your damage was nerfed in 26.22 (Steel Tempest now 100% AD), so early trades are a bit weaker
  • Falls off hard if you die early, because your items do the heavy lifting

Power spikes

  • Level 2: Sweeping Blade + Steel Tempest lets you take your first real trade
  • First item (Blade of The Ruined King): your dueling item, built first in top because fights are long and against high-health enemies
  • Second item (Immortal Shieldbow): survives burst and turns close fights
  • Third item (Infinity Edge): your crits finally hurt, and you become a real split-push threat
  • Top quest done: free Unleashed Teleport and a level cap of 20 for the late game

Top tips

  • Keep your passive shield full before every trade: walk around instead of standing still
  • Exhaust the bruiser the moment they commit, not before
  • Ward your river bush early; you have no partner to warn you about ganks
  • Build Mortal Reminder into healing top laners like Aatrox or Sett
  • Use the top quest's Unleashed Teleport to flank, not to arrive in front of the enemy team
  • Freeze near your tower if you fall behind; Yasuo is weak when he has to walk far forward
  • Remember the 26.22 nerf: your early trades are a little weaker, so respect even matchups
